topic: recalibration on the current on-site H, and the resulting loop ceiling
why: the session-transfer check showed |H| at 8.38 kHz fell from 11.13 dB to 5.15 dB (phase +39.5 deg), so the old model over-predicted that band by about 6 dB and made the loop regenerative there

loop_only_three_arm.note: external source off; the loop is driven only by its own noise

verdict: recalibrating on the current H moved the cancel arm from howling at -6 dB to staying stable at 0 dB and only howling at +3 dB, i.e. roughly +7 dB. The no-model arms are already at the rail near 0 dB. Recalibration, not a coefficient tweak, is what raised the usable gain.
caveat: bypass and cancel_zero should be mathematically identical (both play gain*mic) yet differ by up to 15 dB at -6 dB; that discrepancy is unexplained and must be settled before any ASG number is quoted from these arms
